blocking_findings.title: Final terminal republication leaves its nested custody inventory hash stale
blocking_findings.evidence: Initial TERMINAL.json is durably written at line339. inventory(output) at line342 places that terminal hash and size in custody.supervisor_output_files. After the final budget checkpoint, lines366-369 change final_parent_budget_check and unconditionally rewrite TERMINAL.json. Lines370-373 update the top-level terminal_sha256 and republish custody, but do not refresh the nested inventory row.
blocking_findings.deterministic_normal_path_consequence: On the normal successful path, the first terminal has last_completed_check=after_collection_and_reauthentication and the final terminal has last_completed_check=after_receipt_and_custody_publication. Their contents therefore differ even without a cap failure. The final custody then binds two different hashes for the same unqualified TERMINAL.json path. A verifier treating supervisor_output_files as current custody rejects it or has to ignore the contradictory row.
blocking_findings.required_narrow_closure: Refresh the existing TERMINAL.json row hash/size after the final terminal write before republishing custody, or explicitly type the earlier inventory as a historical snapshot with clear current-custody semantics. No extra cap-check loop, worker/metric/science change or runtime execution is needed.
